benchmark.gold_label_scheme: Each question carries an answer_span; any chunk containing that span is gold. Labels are recomputed per chunking configuration, which is what makes cross-configuration comparison fair and handles overlap honestly.
fairness_controls: both pipelines receive the same raw document and chunk it themselves
the NumPy pipeline is driven through its own split()/embed()/retrieve(), imported not reimplemented
encoder warm in both; embeddings object constructed outside the index timer
benchmark.headline_finding: Chunk size dominates, not the implementation. Within one pipeline, 500->800 chars moves hit@4 by up to 14 points (5 questions); the largest implementation gap at fixed chunk size is 3 points (1 question). The apparent 'NumPy wins' at defaults was a chunking artefact (800/150 vs 1000/200).
caveats_to_state_before_being_asked: n=35, so one question = 2.9 points of hit@4; all implementation gaps are within noise
gold chunks per question varies 1.11-1.31 across configurations, slightly favouring configurations with more gold chunks
single-turn only; the app's retrieve node embeds just the last message, so multi-turn performance is lower than these numbers
retrieval only: generation faithfulness, refusal behaviour and end-to-end latency were NOT measured

resume.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: From-Scratch and Framework Implementations, Benchmarked
resume.rejected_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: From-Scratch Implementation and Deployed Document Assistant
resume.why_rejected: 'Deployed' is false: no Dockerfile, no host config, no public URL, unusable requirements file. The app runs under `streamlit run` on localhost.
bullets: Implemented a RAG retrieval pipeline in NumPy around a MiniLM-384d encoder - overlapping character chunking, unit-normalised embeddings, dot-product cosine search over an (N x 384) matrix, cited context assembly - with no retrieval framework.

Built a transcript QA assistant on LangChain/LangGraph/Streamlit (Chroma, Groq gpt-oss-120b): two-node retrieve->generate graph, SQLite-checkpointed resumable chat threads, txt/pdf/srt/vtt ingestion, map-reduce summarisation under a token-rate cap.

Benchmarked both on a 35-question span-labelled gold set: hit@4 0.86 vs 0.83 at 8-10 ms retrieval, with a chunk-size ablation isolating chunking - not the framework - as the dominant factor, lifting hit@4 to 0.89 and hit@10 to 1.00.

interview_prep.full_list: eval/rag_project_audit_v2.tex sections 6 and 7 (10 questions on the framework app in v1, 5 new ones on the comparison in v2)

hardest_five.q: Your NumPy version beat the framework. Why keep the framework one?
hardest_five.a: The win was a chunking artefact (800/150 vs 1000/200). Holding chunk size fixed, the gap reverses or vanishes; at 800/150 the framework pipeline is best measured (hit@4 0.886, hit@10 1.000). The framework buys capability - PDF/subtitle parsing, persistence, checkpointed threads - not retrieval quality at this scale.
No. One question is 2.9 points at n=35, so that is a single question, inside noise. Only the chunk-size effects (3-5 questions) are defensible.

hardest_five.q: Why is your graph not an agent?
hardest_five.a: Two nodes, three unconditional edges, no tool binding, no conditional routing. The LLM emits text and never influences control flow. If I needed agency the first addition would be a retrieval-grading node with a conditional edge back to query rewriting - the CRAG pattern.

hardest_five.q: What distance metric does your vector store use?
hardest_five.a: Chroma's default l2, not cosine - I set no collection_metadata. Ranking is unaffected because MiniLM output is unit-normalised, so ||a-b||^2 = 2-2cos(theta) is monotonic in cosine. Verified empirically: exact cosine and Chroma return identical rankings on all 35 questions.

hardest_five.q: Chunks are 1000 characters, the encoder takes 256 tokens. Walk me through that.
hardest_five.a: Measured: mean 235 tokens, max 263, 4 of 65 chunks truncated - negligible here, but only because timestamped transcript text has a high chars-per-token ratio. On dense prose the tails would be dropped silently. The correct fix is splitting on the tokeniser, not on characters.
